title: Operating Systems
objectives: Distinguish processes from threads and know when to use each
Explain virtual memory, paging and the TLB
Identify and prevent race conditions and deadlocks

sections.markdown: An operating system (OS) manages hardware and provides services — processes, memory, files, devices, security — to programs through system calls.
An OS is an **airport control tower**: many planes (processes) want the same runways (CPU/memory). The tower schedules them safely so none collide and everyone eventually takes off.

## Process vs Thread
- **Process**: own isolated memory; heavy to create; a crash is contained.
- **Thread**: shares the process's memory; light; great for parallelism but needs synchronization.

## Memory management
- **Virtual memory**: each process sees a private contiguous address space.
- **Paging**: memory split into fixed pages; a page table maps virtual to physical.
- **TLB**: caches recent translations to avoid walking the page table every access.

sections.code:
Deadlock — each thread holds one lock, waits for the other:
  Thread A: lock(X); lock(Y);   // waits for Y
  Thread B: lock(Y); lock(X);   // waits for X  -> DEADLOCK
Fix: always acquire locks in a global order (X then Y).

sections.markdown: **Race condition**: two threads read-modify-write shared state without synchronization, so the result depends on timing (both read balance=100, both add 50, final is 150 not 200).
Prefer high-level primitives (thread pools, channels, async/await) over raw locks. The cheapest lock is the one you never take — minimize shared mutable state.

flashcards.front: Process vs thread in one line?
flashcards.back: Processes have isolated memory; threads share memory within a process.
Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait. Break any one to prevent deadlock.
Caches recent virtual→physical address translations so the CPU avoids walking the page table each access.
Too little RAM causes constant paging to disk, so the system spends all its time swapping instead of working.

quiz.q: Which is TRUE of threads vs processes?
quiz.explain: Threads share their process's address space, which is why they need synchronization.

options: Any one of the four Coffman conditions
quiz.explain: Deadlock needs all four conditions; eliminating any single one prevents it.

quiz.q: A race condition is caused by…
options: Unsynchronized access to shared mutable state
quiz.explain: When threads read-modify-write shared state without coordination, results depend on timing.

options: A private contiguous address space per process
quiz.explain: Each process sees its own virtual address space, mapped to physical pages by the MMU.
